main.job: negating a verbless 'X is Y' sentence (is not / am not)
main.why: Arabic has no present 'is'; ليس is the only way to say 'isn't' in those sentences.
Existence job; used constantly in MSA speech and text.
Arabic has no verb 'have'; this preposition + pronoun does the job.

main.job: was / were: the 'be' of the past
main.why: The present needs no verb, but the past does; A2 learners need it to talk about yesterday.

main.job: turning a statement into a yes/no question
main.why: The standard yes/no question marker in MSA.
Member of the negator set; the everyday present negation.
MSA past negation uses a present form after لم, a key A2 unlock.
Completes the negator set; the only standard way to say 'won't'.
Arabic future = these markers + present verb; one pattern, two spellings (R-TERM-07).
The 'want' job, with the أن + present construction that other modal verbs reuse.

spares.why: Core motion verb with its preposition.

jobs_covered.identity/description: verbless sentence (no term needed); كَانَ for the past
jobs_covered.location: فِي (not taught; A1 preposition, used freely)

shape.notes: Count 10 forces a choice. The negator set (4 members) is complete; must (يَجِبُ أَنْ), can (يَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ) and go (ذَهَبَ) are the next items and sit in spares. Independent pronouns (12 with dual) and the wh-question words (~8) are sets larger than the space left, so they are not started; هَلْ is the yes/no marker, not a wh-word. Politeness is not grammatical in MSA.
